perturbations.failure_summary: Java renders a 231x239 diagram with `Envelope661` as a cluster containing its note and the two root leaves below it. Rust renders a 333x151 diagram, emits `Envelope661` as a plain entity, and solves the root leaves on the same row, consistent with owned-note leakage into the root standalone model.

findings.title: Owned-note-only containers never become SVEK clusters
findings.evidence: The parser records `note.owner` for floating notes (`crates/rustuml-parser/src/parse/deployment.rs:631-637` and `647-652`), but only ordinary node declarations call `add_child` (`815-816` and `851-852`). The renderer then defines `cluster_ids` solely from `node.children` (`crates/rustuml-render/src/deployment.rs:4049-4054`). In `review_root_two_leaves_with_owned_note_leak_ltr.puml`, Java emits `Envelope661` as a cluster; Rust emits it as a plain entity.
findings.interpretation: Any DESCRIPTION container whose only direct child is a floating note falls off the Java cluster path in Rust.

findings.title: Root Magma still treats owned floating notes as root standalones
findings.evidence: `add_deployment_magma_constraints` extends `root_members` with every targetless note regardless of `note.owner` (`crates/rustuml-render/src/deployment.rs:4902-4908`). The fresh `review_root_two_leaves_with_owned_note_leak_ltr.puml` control should give Java a two-leaf root stream plus an inner note, but Rust widens the root solve and produces a materially different canvas and placement.
findings.interpretation: Owned floating notes leak into the root standalone model, so the below-threshold root behavior is still wrong once containers enter the picture.

findings.title: Fresh nested owned-note inputs crash during post-layout slot remapping
findings.evidence: `review_nested_link_before_decl_note_controls_ltr.puml` and `review_nested_three_member_note_control_file_ltr.puml` both panic at `crates/rustuml-render/src/deployment.rs:4238` while remapping `solved_positions`; the first indexes slot 3 with len 3, the second slot 4 with len 3.
findings.interpretation: The revised unified emission model is not total for valid nested DESCRIPTION inputs involving owned notes. At minimum, the node-position remap still assumes a slot inventory that the nested solve does not provide.

findings.title: The simple root-only quark-order path now works on fresh valid controls
findings.interpretation: The rejection is narrower than the whole quark-order idea. The root-only standalone ordering improved, but the owned-note/container model is still incomplete.

findings.title: Java rejects explicit late redeclaration after a link-created alias
findings.evidence: Four exploratory `-pipe` probes showed that `A --> B` followed by later explicit `node B` or `component B` is rejected by Java with `Use 'allowmixing'...` or `This element (B) is already defined`.
findings.interpretation: The preserved link-before-declaration axis uses a valid link-created companion leaf instead of an invalid later explicit redeclaration.

verdict_reason: REJECTED. The implementation does fix the simple root-only emission-order cases, but fresh valid owned-note/container inputs still either diverge or crash. The rejecting evidence is mechanism-shaped: note ownership is recorded in the parser, then dropped from cluster formation, then ignored again by root Magma membership, and the new slot-remapping logic panics on nested owned-note cases. Under the T14 held-out rule, those counterexamples reject the mechanism at Rust revision 082981d1.
